chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"When the slave brings the value of his price after seven years, it is incumbent upon him to accept it."

key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكُ: The slave (male or female) in the context of manumission

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave pays the agreed value for their freedom after seven years?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* establishes the master's obligation to accept the agreed-upon value for manumission (*kitabah*) after the passage of seven years, emphasizing the contractual nature of the process. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the master cannot arbitrarily withhold freedom once the slave fulfills the financial condition, thereby securing the slave's path to liberty. This ruling underscores the ethical imperative of honoring agreements in social transactions within Islamic law.
